summary: Four response-level contrasts cover the clear, teachable errors: a continuing state or description framed as a bounded event (ASP.01); an ongoing action framed as completed or vice versa (ASP.02); a past routine framed as a bounded event or vice versa (ASP.03); and a state/change-of-state verb whose aspect changes its meaning (ASP.04). When a correction is debatable, context is insufficient, or an index mixes distinct contrasts, the assignment is NONE. Unlike v1, these codes describe the local meaning contrast supported by the response, not a presumed learner strategy, L1 transfer, or a global narrative pattern. Duration words and temporal markers are not treated as automatic aspect rules.
left_out: The corrections include many choices that cannot be established as errors from the supplied two sentences alone: descriptive states can sometimes be presented as bounded episodes, and duration or frequency phrases do not force a single aspect. Several entries also mix unrelated corrections, contain unclear wording, or appear to reflect instructor preference; these receive NONE rather than a forced code. I did not create codes for English transfer, narrative flattening, temporal-marker overgeneralization, verb-duration defaults, or patterns across a learner's history: these are learner-level hypotheses, not local meaning contrasts.

taxonomy.name: Continuing state or description vs bounded event
taxonomy.definition: Use when the response clearly describes a past condition, location, identity, possession, evaluation, or other state holding over a reference period, but uses the preterite as though it were a bounded event—or uses the imperfect for a clearly bounded state episode. Do not use for ongoing action verbs (ASP.02), habitual repetition (ASP.03), or a state/change-of-state verb whose aspect specifically changes its lexical meaning (ASP.04). If both aspectual framings are plausible, abstain.
positive_examples: La araña estuvo [estaba] en mi brazo.
El jardín fue [era] grande con muchas plantas.
Me sentía [sentí] inseguro en ese momento.
negative_examples: Ayer estuve en casa de Ana. (A bounded visit, not a continuing background state.)
Cuando era niña, ayudaba a mi madre. (A habitual action; ASP.03.)
taxonomy.distinguishing_probe: Choose the form for a past description holding at a reference time, not a one-time change: «Cuando llegamos, la puerta ___ abierta».

taxonomy.name: Ongoing action vs completed event
taxonomy.definition: Use when context presents an action as in progress or as background at a reference time, but the learner presents it as a completed event, or presents a clearly bounded, completed action as ongoing. Do not use for stable conditions or descriptions (ASP.01), customary repeated actions (ASP.03), or state/change-of-state verbs with a distinct lexical aspectual meaning (ASP.04). A mere duration phrase does not establish the contrast.
positive_examples: Cuando llegaba [llegué] a mi casa, mi abuela estaba enojada. (In the supplied story, this is a single arrival.)
Un día, caminaba por un bosque y escuchaba [escuchó] un sonido.
Luego, hacía [hice] las galletas con chispas de chocolate.
Cuando llamaba [llamé] a mi madre, mi padre me encontró.
negative_examples: Mientras caminaba, sonó el teléfono. (The walk is ongoing background; the phone call is a completed event.)
Todos los días cuidaba a los peces. (A routine, not a single ongoing action; ASP.03.)
taxonomy.distinguishing_probe: Contrast an action in progress with a bounded event: «Mientras ___ (cocinar), sonó la alarma».

taxonomy.name: Past routine vs bounded occurrence or series
taxonomy.definition: Use when context clearly presents customary, habitual, or regularly repeated past activity, but the learner frames it as a bounded occurrence or completed series, or when a clearly bounded occurrence/series is framed as a routine. Do not use merely because a sentence contains a frequency word; a repeated set can be presented as completed. Do not use for a one-time ongoing action (ASP.02) or a state verb whose aspect changes meaning (ASP.04).
positive_examples: Cuando era niña, mi mamá me ayudó [ayudaba] con mi tarea.
Cuando éramos niñas siempre hicimos [hacíamos] todo juntas.
En verano iban a la playa y se divirtieron [divertían] mucho juntos.
negative_examples: Fui tres veces al cine la semana pasada. (A bounded, counted set of completed visits.)
Ayer cuidé a los peces por una hora. (A bounded occasion, not a customary routine.)
taxonomy.distinguishing_probe: Decide whether the sentence describes a routine or a completed set: «En aquella época, todos los domingos ___ (visitar) a mis abuelos».

taxonomy.name: State meaning vs onset, result, or successful event
taxonomy.definition: Use only when context clearly establishes the lexical contrast for a state/change-of-state verb—such as saber, conocer, querer, poder, necesitar, or darse cuenta—and the learner's aspect selects the other reading. Examples include continuing knowledge vs finding out, ongoing ability vs managing to do something, or continuing desire vs deciding/trying on a particular occasion. Do not infer a general learner rule from one error; do not use if the context does not establish the intended reading. For ordinary action verbs, use ASP.02 or ASP.03.
positive_examples: No pude [podía] dormir. (In the supplied context, inability continued.)
Sus padres no supieron [sabían] cómo ayudar a su hija.
Pedí ir a casa porque quise [quería] ir a casa y comer fresas.
No me daba [di] cuenta de que estaba describiendo mi pasado.
negative_examples: Por fin supe la respuesta. (A bounded discovery; preterite is appropriate.)
Podía nadar cuando era niña. (Ongoing ability; imperfect is appropriate.)
taxonomy.distinguishing_probe: Choose the form that means «finally found out»: «Ayer por fin ___ la verdad».
